title: The periods of the last 539 million years
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: These twelve periods are the story of complex life, from the first animals with shells to today. They are the names you see in museums, on fossil labels and in dinosaur books.

How to hold it: Use a first-letter sentence for the order: "Cows Often Sit Down Calmly; Perhaps To Just Chew Peacefully, Not Quickly." Then chunk by era: six Paleozoic periods (old life), three Mesozoic (dinosaurs), three Cenozoic (mammals). Give each period one picture from the 'what lived' column and place them along a long hallway, oldest by the front door. Learn the order first; add the start dates once the order is solid.
